why: GET /v1/jobs and /v1/jobs/:id on qnfo-ops are bearer-gated. This file is a public, key-free mirror of job STATUS metadata. It is a snapshot, not a live endpoint.
source: qnfo-audit D1, table ops_jobs (read via the ops endpoint's read-only SQL path)
schema: CREATE TABLE ops_jobs (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued', model TEXT, strategy TEXT, payload TEXT, response TEXT, tool_log TEXT, error TEXT, created_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT)
how_to_tell_if_a_job_succeeded: Read status. But status alone misleads on ~40% of rows - see D17.
response_chars > 0 means the leg produced output. Read it.
Grep the response body for 'INCOMPLETE:' - that, not status, decides task completion.
Treat 'continuing' as 'leg done, chain handed off'. Check the NEWEST job for that chain, not the id you were handed.
updated_at advances only at the terminal transition, not during the run. Compare elapsed_s against the observed max (801.457 s) to judge a stall.
7 of 8 failed rows carry no error text. You can learn THAT it failed, never WHY.
tool_log truncates at 3,000 chars, so the job record is not a complete account of what the job did.
There is no parent_id / chain_id / depth column, so a multi-leg chain cannot be followed by query.

redaction.reason: response and payload carry fleet internals and the client's replayed conversation; this file is public and indexable. The spec's publicJobView redacts payload only; this mirror redacts response too, deliberately.

succeeded.note: leg returned; may still carry an INCOMPLETE trailer

continuing.note: answer already written, terminal status never set (D17)

running.note: all under 2.5 min old at snapshot time

corrected_claim_updated_at.previous_claim: updated_at is set once at pickup and never advanced, so a hung job is indistinguishable from a healthy one.
corrected_claim_updated_at.accurate_statement: updated_at is written at pickup and again at the terminal transition, but NOT as a heartbeat during the run. A stall is detectable by elapsed time, not by updated_at alone.
corrected_claim_updated_at.none_were_stuck: All four transitioned out of 'running'. The previous 'indeterminate by construction' verdict is resolved by observation: they were genuinely in flight.

snapshot_drift: The mirror is self-perturbing - every invocation of the ops endpoint writes an ops_jobs row, so any snapshot of this table is stale within minutes and can never be a consistent read. This snapshot is itself an instance: the five 'running' rows were created by the very session that wrote this file. Treat the numbers as indicative, never as a settled count.
known_defect: D17: 42 rows hold status='continuing' with a finished answer already written. The terminal status is never written in the same statement as response, so any poller reads 'continuing' forever. The count grew 39 -> 42 between 13:45:33Z and 13:49:23Z while succeeded grew only 47 -> 48. A public status surface is functionally useless until D17 is fixed.
known_defect_related: D18: the same missing terminal write causes the durable path to re-execute an identical prompt (3x observed on two attachments), multiplying compute and re-running any non-idempotent side effect inside a job.
